ai.description: Don's Golden-backed Frog reaches 40–50 mm. It features a bright golden-yellow dorsum, dark lateral bands, and a distinct white upper lip stripe. Long, slender limbs aid in rapid jumping.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana doni* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white upper lip stripe that extends clearly to the shoulder, unlike similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: Hylarana doni inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams and rocky areas at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Don's Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small insects among the leaf litter and vegetation near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana doni* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of eggs in stagnant or slow-moving water bodies. Further specific reproductive data remains limited.
ai.distributionRemarks: Hylarana doni is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting the evergreen forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800–1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Hylarana doni* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically emitted from vegetation near slow-moving forest streams.
